projects.title: Huli
projects.tagline: Unannounced action project with public scope around gameplay, combat, content, and camera design.
projects.summary: HULI is an unannounced dark-fantasy action project inspired by Fengshen Yanyi. The public portfolio scope stays intentionally high level: gameplay, combat, content, and camera design work that can be discussed without revealing production details.
projects.cardSummary: Unannounced action project focused on gameplay, combat, content, and camera design within a dark fantasy setting.
contributions: Contributed to gameplay, combat, content, and camera design within the public-safe project scope.
Created design documentation and prototypes to clarify feature intent before implementation discussion.
Worked cross-functionally to refine systems through playtest feedback and production constraints.

systems.title: Public scope
items: Gameplay and combat design work described at a role level.
Content and camera design framed without unreleased implementation detail.
Documentation and prototype support for feature direction.

results: Combat, content, and camera intent was documented and prototyped before implementation started.
Feature designs were refined against playtest feedback and production constraints.
projects.problem: Because the project is unannounced, the case study needs to show role scope without exposing confidential systems, unreleased content, or production outcomes.

projects.title: Space Conqueror
projects.tagline: Voxel combat prototype with single-player pacing and multiplayer hooks.
projects.summary: Space Conqueror is a space-themed action prototype where I explored combat feel, enemy behavior, encounter pacing, and technical systems needed for both solo and networked play.
projects.cardSummary: Space-themed combat prototype focused on encounter pacing, enemy behavior, and multiplayer-ready systems.
projects.problem: I wanted a portfolio piece that showed I could handle more than visual presentation: combat tuning, AI behavior, resource management, and the technical groundwork for multiplayer needed to come together in one readable case study.
contributions: Designed the core combat loop and enemy encounter structure.
Built and iterated on level flow, pacing, and prototype layout.
Implemented enemy AI using a finite state machine.
Added object pooling, URP optimization, and cross-platform support.
Integrated multiplayer systems using Photon PUN and player services through PlayFab.

systems.title: Combat and Encounter Design
items: Defined enemy composition, wave structure, and retreat or pressure moments.
Balanced player movement and survivability around fast readability.
Used space layout as part of difficulty shaping rather than only visual dressing.

systems.title: Technical Implementation
items: Implemented enemy state logic with a finite state machine.
Used object pooling to reduce runtime allocation spikes.
Prepared the prototype for PC and WebGL delivery.

systems.title: Online Systems
items: Integrated Photon PUN for real-time multiplayer support.
Connected player-facing services with Azure PlayFab.
Used the project to bridge design intention and engineering constraints.

results: Produced a portfolio project that demonstrates both design thinking and implementation depth.
Finished a playable build with a recorded gameplay demo.
Learned where multiplayer complexity changes scope and design priorities early.

gallery.description: Hero artwork used across the case study and project explorer.

projects.title: Lunarfall
projects.tagline: Dark-fantasy pixel strategy that fuses real-time strategy with action combat.
projects.summary: Lunarfall: Pixel Strategy is an ongoing personal project that blends RTS production and unit control with action combat. The design lives in a spreadsheet GDD: unit roles and unlock conditions, combat stats, and a currency economy mapped by sources, sinks, and caps, alongside pixel-art town and menu mockups.
projects.cardSummary: RTS-meets-action pixel strategy concept designed through a spreadsheet GDD, unit balance sheets, and economy planning.
projects.problem: Mixing RTS and action asks one player to be both commander and fighter. The design has to keep production planning and moment-to-moment combat readable on a small screen without one loop starving the other.
contributions: Wrote the sample GDD as a structured spreadsheet covering units, combat attributes, and progression.
Defined unit roles, unlock conditions, and combat behaviors across the roster.
Planned the progression economy with explicit currency sources, sinks, and caps.
Mocked up the town hub and menu screens in pixel art to test tone and information layout.

systems.title: Units and Economy
items: The roster splits production and melee roles, each with unlock states and combat attributes.
The currency sheet tracks where each resource enters and leaves the economy, with caps to stop hoarding.
Balance values live in one sheet so every tuning pass stays traceable.

results: A working GDD that defines the roster, combat stats, and economy before production code.
A clear base for the next step: prototyping the RTS-action combat loop.

projects.title: FarmMatch
projects.tagline: Cute animal matching puzzle for portrait mobile, with boards built around blockers and level goals.
projects.summary: FarmMatch is a casual animal-matching puzzle for portrait mobile. The board captures show the level design work: arrangements of animal pieces, blockers, and goals that change from level to level to keep a simple matching loop fresh.
projects.cardSummary: Cute animal matching project with portrait-mobile puzzle boards and a bright casual presentation.
projects.problem: A matching puzzle repeats one action thousands of times. Variety has to come from the board itself: where blockers sit, which goals are set, and how pieces are arranged, while the screen stays readable at a glance.
contributions: Designed board layouts that combine animal pieces, blockers, and level goals.
Varied goals and blocker placement to pace difficulty across the level set.
Kept boards readable in portrait so players can spot matches quickly.

systems.title: Board and Level Design
items: Blockers decide which matches are open on each board.
Every level has a clear goal, so players always know what clears it.
Bright, distinct animal pieces keep matches easy to read on a phone.

results: A level set where boards and goals change steadily from level to level.
Practice pacing a simple loop through level design instead of adding new rules.

projects.title: GoodSort
projects.tagline: Portrait shelf-sorting puzzle focused on readability, satisfying organization, and scalable level pacing.
projects.summary: GoodSort is a portrait-mobile sorting puzzle where I focused on making the shelf layout readable at a glance, keeping the interaction satisfying, and shaping progression that could expand through many level variations. The project centers on a simple organizing fantasy, then builds challenge through blocker placement, board composition, and content pacing instead of overcomplicating the core loop.
projects.cardSummary: Portrait shelf-sorting puzzle built around readable boards, satisfying organization, and scalable level variation.
projects.problem: GoodSort needed a sorting loop that felt immediately readable on a phone-sized screen while still leaving room for blocker variety, level escalation, and a progression structure that could support a larger content library.
contributions: Defined the core shelf-sorting loop around quick visual grouping and low-friction portrait interaction.
Shaped board readability through clearer product grouping, blocker placement, and level composition.
Built a stronger foundation for future content iteration by keeping the puzzle rules approachable while leaving room for deeper progression pacing.

systems.title: Puzzle Readability And Pacing
items: Centered the design on a simple organization fantasy that players could understand quickly in portrait play.
Used shelf layouts, blocker combinations, and grouping logic to create level variety without losing visual clarity.
Kept the core rules approachable so the project could scale through content pacing rather than system bloat.

results: Validated GoodSort as a clear, approachable sorting concept with enough depth to justify further iteration.
Created a stronger design foundation for expanding level variety, progression pacing, and content volume.

projects.title: Satisdom
projects.tagline: Relaxing satisfying-game concept built from bite-size beauty-care and tidy-up interactions.
projects.summary: Satisdom is a mobile satisfying-game concept made of short, relaxing micro-tasks. The design work runs from hand-drawn before-and-after concept frames to mini-game flow notes, content planning sheets, and sound-feedback reviews, so every action lands with a satisfying payoff.
projects.cardSummary: Satisfying micro-task concept designed through before-and-after sketches, flow notes, and sound-feedback reviews.
projects.problem: Satisfying games have almost no challenge, so the feeling is the product. Each micro-task needs a clear before state, a tactile action, and a visible, audible payoff, all within a few seconds.
contributions: Sketched before-and-after concept frames for each relaxing interaction.
Mapped mini-game flows so every task has a clear start, action, and payoff.
Planned the content list and task variety in spreadsheets.
Reviewed sound effects against each action to strengthen the feedback.

systems.title: Interaction Feel
items: Each task shows the mess first, so the cleanup reads as progress.
Short actions keep sessions relaxing and easy to repeat.
Audio cues are checked against each interaction so the payoff feels physical.

results: A documented set of micro-task interactions ready for prototyping.
A repeatable sketch, flow, and sound process for designing satisfying moments.

projects.title: Screw
projects.tagline: Unscrew-style color puzzle: level design, difficulty ramp, and data-driven balancing for a live mobile title.
projects.summary: Screw is a mobile unscrew puzzle I worked on as a Game Designer at Rainbow 5s. My work covered level design, screw-color sequencing and the difficulty ramp across the level set, and tracking sheets used to audit coverage, surface outlier levels, and plan batch balancing passes.
projects.cardSummary: Unscrew-style color puzzle with designed level boards and tracking sheets used to rebalance difficulty in batches.
projects.problem: Unscrew puzzles depend on readability: players must see which screws pin which plates and which colors come next. The level set needed a steady difficulty ramp that kept sessions satisfying while supporting rewarded-ad and retention goals.
contributions: Designed level boards, composing plates, screws, and color order to shape each puzzle.
Sequenced screw colors and overlaps to build a deliberate difficulty ramp across the level set.
Built tracking sheets to audit level coverage and flag outliers for rebalancing.
Used A/B tests and player metrics to tune balance between batches.

systems.title: Level Design and Balancing
items: Board composition controls how deeply each screw color is buried.
Difficulty ramps through color count, overlap depth, and how many moves stay open.
Balancing passes are planned in batches from tracked data, not one-off tweaks.

results: A level set with a readable, gradual difficulty curve.
A repeatable data-review process for rebalancing levels in batches.

projects.title: Tank
projects.tagline: Arcade tank battler for mobile, tuned for rewarded ads, revenue, and retention.
projects.summary: Tank is an arcade tank-battle mobile game I worked on as a Game Designer at Rainbow 5s. My work focused on improvements aimed at rewarded-ad engagement, revenue, and retention, plus level design and balance tuning informed by A/B tests and player metrics.
projects.cardSummary: Arcade mobile tank battler where I worked on retention, rewarded-ad improvements, and balance tuning.
projects.problem: A live arcade game has to earn from rewarded ads without breaking the fun of the fight. Every ad offer needs to feel like a reward the player wants, and balance changes need proof before they ship.
contributions: Proposed improvements to raise rewarded-ad engagement, revenue, and retention.
Designed and tuned levels for the live game.
Ran A/B tests and analyzed metrics to adjust game balance.

systems.title: Live Optimization
items: Rewarded-ad offers sit at moments where players already want a boost.
Balance changes are tested with A/B splits before they roll out.
Results are read against retention and revenue goals.

results: Contributed improvements aimed at rewarded-ad, revenue, and retention metrics.
Hands-on experience running A/B tests on a live mobile title.

projects.title: Horror Carnival
projects.tagline: Horror carnival puzzle prototype built in Unity, inspired by Goods Master.
projects.summary: Horror Carnival Puzzle is a personal prototype from September 2024, inspired by Goods Master and set in a creepy carnival. Levels are split into haunted rooms with ally and enemy characters, a round timer, and a booster to call in more allies. I built it in Unity and recorded a gameplay demo.
projects.problem: Puzzle games in the Goods Master mold are calm and tidy, while a horror carnival is tense and busy. The prototype had to bring in that mood without making the board harder to read.
contributions: Designed the puzzle levels and the haunted carnival room layout.
Built the prototype in Unity, including ally and enemy characters and the level flow.
Recorded a gameplay demo of the finished prototype.
